issues.description: The UML and problem description specify the lecture attributes as private (negative sign in UML), and the solution implementation declares these attributes as private, but the template file pre-defines two attributes (lectureName and numberOfInscribedStudents) as public. This visibility mismatch between the template and the UML/solution can confuse students about the intended access level for attributes and whether they should make fields private and provide getters/setters.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's pre-declared attributes use the same visibility as the UML and solution (change the public fields in the template to private) or add a clarifying comment in the template that students should implement attributes as private. This keeps the template aligned with the UML and the reference solution and avoids confusion about intended access levels.
